text:
incident-bot: ALARM: prod inference latency SLO breach (p95 > 450ms) in us-east-1 for 6m. auto-escalate to #incidents and page oncall-sre. metrics: https://metrics.redwood/prod/latency?s=us-east-1 :rotating_light:
pranav: ack — I’m oncall SRE. grabbing context, paging runtime and platform. please add logs/traces here.
jess: seeing a big increase in downstream slow tails. streaming frames are failing with 503s and some clients dropping. stack traces show KV cache thrash + high GPU enqueue latency. logs: `stream-error: connection reset by peer`, `enqueue-time > 120ms`.
sam: also seeing a spike in continuous-batching queue depth. hypothesis: streaming long-lived connections are preventing efficient batching -> backlog -> high latency for non-streaming requests.
morgan: heads-up from GTM/support — a few high-volume customers reported partial failures in chat UIs, some saw fallback to polling. need to confirm blast radius before any mitigation.
pranav: plan proposal — soft mitigation first: temporarily disable streaming responses as a feature gate for prod globally OR route streaming to lower-priority capacity tier; also reduce per-key concurrent streams. prefer quick toggle to stabilize. any objections?
jess: +1 for toggle. if we disable streaming we need to ensure server returns non-streaming buffered responses (same model) so clients see a single final response. communicate immediately to support.
sam: two tactical ops we can do in parallel: 1) apply request-level rate limiting for streaming endpoints from 100r/s -> 50r/s, and 2) flip feature gate `streaming_responses` to off for prod canary then roll. I'll run the commands, need approvals.
pranav: do the canary in us-east-1 only. if stable 5m, roll worldwide. morgan please prep support blurb that explains degraded UX (no streaming) but preserved completions.
morgan: on it — draft: "We're temporarily disabling streaming output to stabilize response reliability. Users will receive full responses once available instead of incremental updates. No user data is affected." will share to #support for review. :white_check_mark:
sam: executing canary — command:
```
# feature toggle service
rbctl feature set streaming_responses --env prod --region us-east-1 --value off --canary 10%
```
deploy-bot: runbook: starting feature toggle: rbctl v1.14.2; initiating canary 10% in us-east-1. request id: rb-2026-11-15-0001
deploy-bot: canary applied to 8 instances in us-east-1 (ids: i-0a1b2c3d..).
pranav: monitoring key signals: p95 latency, enqueue time, GPU utilization, streaming-error-rate. setting alerts to auto-escalate if p95 rises > 20% over baseline after toggle.
sam: additionally reducing streaming endpoint rate limit for prod globally:
```
# ratelimit service
ratelimitctl update --service streaming-api --limit 50rps --scope global --duration 30m --reason "incident mitigation"
```
deploy-bot: ratelimit update accepted, change id rl-3345.
jess: initial observation after canary (2m): p95 down ~18% in canary nodes, streaming-error-rate down 65% on those instances. overall region p95 down ~7%. good sign.
morgan: support notified, posted pinned message to status page draft. also prepping outbound to 10 customers on the active list that saw errors.
elaine: FYI: a downstream consumer (partner-x) uses SSE long-lived streams; they may see immediate reconnects. we should pre-warn them.
pranav: agree, draft sent to partner-x. ops checklist: 1) monitor for 10 minutes post-rollout, 2) if stable, increment canary to 50% then 100% (target 20m total), 3) keep rate limit in place for 30m after full roll, 4) create postmortem ticket.
sam: canary -> 50% now. command: `rbctl feature set streaming_responses --env prod --region us-east-1 --value off --canary 50%`
deploy-bot: canary updated -> 50% (instances updated).
pranav: metrics at +12m from start: p95 us-east-1 down 28% vs peak, enqueue-time improved, GPU queue shorter. overall throughput stable.
jess: no major regressions observed. non-streaming latency slightly higher for some short queries (clients now wait for full response) but overall user-facing errors dropped to near-zero.
morgan: posting customer note to status.redwood.com: "Degraded streaming temporarily disabled to restore service stability. We expect minimal functional impact aside from no incremental updates; full responses will be delivered." posting now. :loudspeaker:
pranav: going to roll to global regions in 2m if metrics hold. any objections?
sam: no objections. rolling global.
deploy-bot: feature toggle applied globally off for prod. request id rb-2026-11-15-0002.
pranav: global metrics 5m after full roll: p95 down ~22% vs pre-mitigation, error-rate on streaming endpoint -> 0.8% from 6.2%. GPU enqueue latency back to normal band.
eljunk: (typo)
jess: small note — some mobile clients treat lack of SSE as error; we should ensure SDKs handle fallbacks gracefully, open ticket for SDK team.
morgan: support update sent to affected customers, CS will proactively reach out to top-tier ones.
pranav: immediate mitigation successful. now next steps: revert ratelimit to previous after 30m if stable, schedule postmortem, and build an automated degraded-mode policy for streaming to auto-fallback in future. also we need to investigate root cause: why streaming connections were starving batch paths — likely KV cache misuse + scheduling priority bug.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: severity downgraded from Sev2 -> Sev3 at 1945678950. reason: mitigation stabilized performance, customer impact reduced.
pranav: capturing timeline and actions in incident ticket: INC-2026-845. please add logs, traces, and any reproductions.
jess: adding a quick reproduction script to the ticket that simulates many concurrent streaming clients.
elaine: tagging SRE and runtime for a deeper post-incident review. proposed owners: sam (runtime), jess (platform), pranav (oncall).
pranav: thanks team. final note: do not re-enable streaming until we've validated scheduling fix + canary on staging for 24h. assigning follow-ups. :heavy_check_mark:
